DESCRIPTION:
FACS of adipocyte precursor cells from adipose tissue (mouse or human)

We dissociate adipose tissue of mouse or human origin and perform FACS to isolate adipocyte precursor cells. The cells are sorted in a FACS Aria II instrument using a 100 um nozzle. 

Depending on the type of adipose depot, cell viability at the end of the sorting process is about 60-80%. We have data demonstrating high adipocyte differentiation from the sorted precursor cells, indicating high purity level. We have also successfully expanded these cells in vitro and also used them immediately after sorting for complex applications including transcriptome analysis.

DESCRIPTION: Glucocerebrosides are formed by the tethering of glucose to a ceramide by glucosylceramide synthase. They are present in neuronal and non-neuronal mammalian tissues and are found at low quantities in a large number of plant species. Glucocerebrosides are precursors in the synthesis of lactosylceramides and gangliosides. Increased levels of glucocerebrosides are associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in mice and with neuronal deficits observed in neuronopathic Gaucher disease. This product is a mixture of glucocerebrosides, with variable ceramide chain lengths, isolated from a spleen of a human with Gaucher's disease.

DESCRIPTION: Glucocerebrosides are formed by the tethering of glucose to a ceramide by glucosylceramide synthase. They are present in neuronal and non-neuronal mammalian tissues and are found at low quantities in a large number of plant species. Glucocerebrosides are precursors in the synthesis of lactosylceramides and gangliosides. Increased levels of glucocerebrosides are associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in mice and with neuronal deficits observed in neuronopathic Gaucher disease. This product is a mixture of glucocerebrosides, with variable ceramide chain lengths, isolated from a spleen of a human with Gaucher's disease.

Glucocerebrosides are precursors in the synthesis of lactosylceramides and gangliosides. Increased levels of glucocerebrosides are associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in mice and with neuronal deficits observed in neuronopathic Gaucher disease. This product is a mixture of glucocerebrosides, with variable ceramide chain lengths, isolated from a spleen of a human with Gaucher's disease.

DESCRIPTION: Glucocerebrosides are formed by the tethering of glucose to a ceramide by glucosylceramide synthase. Increased levels of glucocerebrosides are associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in mice and with neuronal deficits observed in neuronopathic Gaucher disease. This product is a mixture of glucocerebrosides, with variable ceramide chain lengths, isolated from a spleen of a human with Gaucher's disease.

Ocular transplantation a surgical procedure where a damaged or diseased cornea (the transparent, front part of the eye that covers the iris and pupil) is replaced with healthy corneal tissue from a donor. Infectious keratitis is a serious and potentially sight-threatening condition characterized by inflammation of the cornea due to an infection. It can be caused by bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites.
